sentences.ko: 요즘 매일 아침 네 시에 깨는데, 그러고는 그냥 누운 채로 아홉 시 전에는 어차피 손도 못 대는 회사 일을 머릿속으로 계속 굴려요. 오후 두 시쯤까지는 괜찮다가 그다음부터는 아무짝에도 쓸모가 없고요. 더 일찍 자 봤는데, 그래 봐야 누워 있는 시간만 늘었어요.
sentences.text: I've been waking up at four every morning and then I just lie there running through work stuff in my head that I can't do anything about until nine anyway. And I'm okay until about two in the afternoon, and then I'm useless. I tried going to bed earlier, and all that did was give me more hours to lie there.

alts.text: Four in the morning, every morning, that is when I am up, and then I just lie there going over work stuff I cannot touch until nine anyway. I'm fine till about two in the afternoon, and after that I'm useless. I tried getting to bed earlier and all that did was give me more hours to lie there.

I have been waking at four o'clock every morning, and I then lie there going over matters of work in my head that I cannot address until nine in any case. I am well enough until approximately two in the afternoon, after which I am of no use. I tried going to bed earlier, and the only result was additional hours spent lying awake.

sentences.note: **running through work stuff in my head** 는 머릿속으로 일을 계속 되짚어 굴린다는 뜻입니다. **all that did was ~** 는 해 봤자 결과가 그것뿐이었다고 할 때 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 토요일에 잡아 둔 약속이 두 개 있었는데 둘 다 취소했어요. 그런데 하나도 미안하지가 않네요. 커피를 두 번 내려 마셨고, 책은 네 쪽쯤 읽었고, 오후에는 애처럼 잠들어 버렸어요. 금요일에 물어봤으면 할 일 없으면 답답해서 못 견딘다고 했을 텐데, 몇 주 만에 제일 좋았어요.
sentences.text: We had two things on the calendar Saturday and I canceled both of them, and I don't feel bad about it at all. I made coffee twice, I got through maybe four pages of a book, and I fell asleep in the afternoon like a kid. If you'd asked me Friday I would have told you I'd lose my mind with nothing to do, but it was the best I've felt in weeks.

alts.text: Saturday we had two things booked and I canceled both, and honestly, zero guilt. I made coffee twice, got maybe four pages into a book, and I konked out in the afternoon like a kid. Ask me on Friday and I'd have said I'd go out of my mind with nothing to do, but I haven't felt that good in weeks.

We had two engagements scheduled for Saturday and I canceled both of them, and I do not regret it in the least. I made coffee twice, I read perhaps four pages of a book, and I fell asleep in the afternoon in the manner of a child. Had you asked me on Friday, I would have told you that I would lose my mind with nothing to do, but it was the best I have felt in weeks.

sentences.note: **lose my mind** 는 답답하거나 지루해서 미쳐 버릴 것 같다는 말입니다. **the best I've felt in weeks** 처럼 최상급 뒤에 기간을 붙이면 몇 주 만에 제일 좋다는 뜻이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 그 사람은 우리 남편 회사 친구인데, 진짜 웃겨요. 다들 그렇게 말한다는 거 알아요. 그런데 이건 알아 두세요, 처음 이십 분은 말이 없어요. 그러니까 음식 나오기 전에 아니다 싶어 접지 마세요. 그리고 얼마 전에 강아지를 들였대요. 그러니 잘 안 풀려도 이야깃거리 하나는 있는 셈이에요.
sentences.text: So he's my husband's friend from work, and he's actually funny, which I know is what everybody says. But here's the thing, he's quiet for the first twenty minutes, so don't write him off before the food comes. And he just got a dog, so if it goes badly you've at least got something to talk about.

alts.text: Okay so he works with my husband, and he is genuinely funny, which yeah, that's what everybody says. But here's the thing, he's quiet for like the first twenty minutes, so don't count him out before the food shows up. And he just got a dog, so worst case you've got something to talk about.

He is a friend of my husband from work, and he is genuinely amusing, which I am aware is what everyone says. I should mention, however, that he is quiet for the first twenty minutes, so please do not dismiss him before the food arrives. He has also recently acquired a dog, so if the evening goes badly you will at least have something to discuss.

sentences.note: **here's the thing** 은 정작 중요한 말을 꺼낼 때 쓰는 말머리입니다. **write him off** 는 가망 없다고 미리 제쳐 둔다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 세 군데를 들어가 봤는데 전부 자리가 꽉 찼더라고요. 마지막 집에서는 어떤 남자가 한 테이블에 노트북을 놓고 그 옆 테이블에 가방을 올려놨어요. 눈치챌 만큼 오래 옆에 서 있었는데 끝까지 알아채지를 않더라고요. 결국 우리 집 식탁으로 돌아왔어요. 애초에 여기서 시작했어야 했는데 말이죠.
sentences.text: I walked into three places and every one of them was full, and at the last one there was a guy with his laptop on one table and his bag on the table next to it. So I stood there long enough that he should have noticed, and he just didn't. I ended up back at my own kitchen table, which is where I should have started.

alts.text: Three places I tried, and every single one was packed, and at the last one this guy had his laptop on one table and his bag on the table next to it. I stood there long enough that he should've clocked me, and he just didn't. I wound up back at my own kitchen table, which is where I should've started.

I went into three establishments and every one of them was full, and at the last of them there was a man with his laptop on one table and his bag on the table beside it. I stood there long enough that he ought to have noticed, and he simply did not. I ended up back at my own kitchen table, which is where I should have begun.

sentences.note: **ended up** 은 이러저러하다가 결국 어떻게 되었다고 할 때 씁니다. **should have started** 처럼 should have 를 쓰면 그렇게 했어야 했는데 안 했다는 후회가 됩니다.

sentences.ko: 4월에 기타를 샀어요. 이번에는 꼭 배우려고요. 진짜로 한 달쯤은 꾸준히 했어요. 그러다 손가락이 아파서 한 주를 걸렀는데, 한 주 거르면 사실상 거기서 끝이에요. 지금도 눈에 보이라고 서랍장에 기대 세워 뒀어요. 그거 보면 미안해서라도 치겠지 싶었거든요. 그런데 이제는 눈에 들어오지도 않네요.
sentences.text: I bought a guitar in April because I was finally going to learn, and I actually stuck with it for about a month. Then my fingers hurt and I skipped a week, and once you skip a week that's kind of it. It's still leaning against the dresser where I can see it, because I thought that would guilt me into playing it, but now I don't even see it anymore.

alts.text: Back in April I got a guitar because I was finally gonna learn, and I actually kept it up for about a month. Then my fingers hurt and I skipped a week, and once you skip a week that's pretty much that. It's still propped against the dresser where I can see it, because I figured that'd guilt me into playing it, but now I don't even see it anymore.

I purchased a guitar in April because I intended at last to learn, and I did in fact keep at it for about a month. Then my fingers became sore and I missed a week, and once one misses a week, that is more or less the end of it. It is still leaning against the dresser where I can see it, because I thought that would shame me into playing it, but at this point I no longer notice it.

sentences.note: **stuck with it** 은 지겨워도 그만두지 않고 계속했다는 뜻입니다. **guilt me into playing it** 처럼 guilt 를 동사로 쓰면 미안한 마음이 들게 해서 하게 만든다는 말이 됩니다.
